fullName.value: Inactive tyrosine-protein kinase transmembrane receptor ROR1

texts.value: Has very low kinase activity in vitro and is unlikely to function as a tyrosine kinase in vivo (PubMed:25029443). Receptor for ligand WNT5A which activates downstream NFkB signaling pathway and may result in the inhibition of WNT3A-mediated signaling (PubMed:25029443, PubMed:27162350). In the inner ear, crucial for spiral ganglion neurons to innervate auditory hair cells (PubMed:27162350). Via IGFBP5 ligand, forms a complex with ERBB2 to enhance CREB oncogenic signaling (PubMed:36949068)

Expressed strongly in human heart, lung and kidney, but weakly in the CNS. Isoform Short is strongly expressed in fetal and adult CNS and in a variety of human cancers, including those originating from CNS or PNS neuroectoderm
Expressed at high levels during early embryonic development. The expression levels drop strongly around day 16 and there are only very low levels in adult tissues

The activation loop of the kinase domain adopts an inactive conformation and the ATP-binding pocket is occluded and inaccessible (PubMed:32619402). Despite lacking kinase activity, the kinase domain is required for signaling (PubMed:32619402)

disease.description: A form of non-syndromic sensorineural hearing loss. Sensorineural deafness results from damage to the neural receptors of the inner ear, the nerve pathways to the brain, or the area of the brain that receives sound information.

texts.value: The disease is caused by variants affecting the gene represented in this entry
Belongs to the protein kinase superfamily. Tyr protein kinase family. ROR subfamily
The kinase domain has very low catalytic activity in vitro (PubMed:25029443). Does not bind ATP (PubMed:24107129, PubMed:32619402)
